712.note: Family-owned Chandler Mexican restaurant serving since 1974, now run by founder Elmer's children.

4518.note: Desert lodge restaurant run since 1937, when a husband and wife bought the lodge; James Beard Foundation America's Classics honoree (2005).
4518.fn: The lodge has been a restaurant since its owners bought it in 1937.

5223.note: Taquería from chef René Andrade; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand (2026).

5241.note: Steakhouse founded in 1950 by Jack Durant on Central Avenue, known for its crimson booths; on The New York Times's 2026 restaurant list (its own site).
5241.fn: Founded 1950 on Central Avenue; the sources don't say it has always been at this address.

5267.jbf: Outstanding Professional in Beverage Service semifinalist 2026 (Ross Simon)

5353.note: Taco shop in the "heritage-driven Sonoran cooking" vein (PHOENIX magazine, 2025): mesquite-grilled carne asada with wild chiltepin peppers.

5370.note: Wood-fired Sonoran cuisine (MICHELIN Guide) from chef René Andrade, the 2026 MICHELIN Guide Southwest Young Chef Award winner.

5514.note: Night-only Sonoran dog stand on the southwest corner of 20th Street and Indian School Road (Nogales No. 2 truck, serving since 2001); street number from Edible Phoenix (2008).

5756.note: Founded in 1992 by the late Tohono O'odham chef Cecelia Miller (KJZZ); James Beard America's Classics honoree (2012) and MICHELIN Recommended (2026). Now co-owned by Jennifer Miller and Richard Perry.
5756.fn: Founded 1992; the sources don't say whether it has always been at this address.

5764.note: Bugarin family restaurant opened in 1970 serving Sonoran-style Mexican food; it calls itself "The Home of the Chimichanga" and says it was the first to top the chimichanga with sour cream, guacamole, tomatoes, onions and cheese (its own claim).
5764.fn: Opened 1970; the sources don't say whether it was always at this address.

5855.note: Family-owned Chihuahua-style taco restaurant; James Beard Award semifinalist (2026). A second shop is in Mesa.
5855.jbf: Best Chef: Southwest semifinalist 2026 (Armando Hernandez and Nadia Holguin)

5877.jbf: Outstanding Professional in Beverage Service semifinalist 2026 (Zac Adcox)

6671.note: Late-night Phoenix Sonoran dog stand; owner Aureliano Dominguez started with a borrowed cart around 1990 (The Arizona Republic, via Hoodline). Four west Phoenix locations, closed Mondays.
6671.fn: Started around 1990 with a borrowed cart.

6857.note: Family Mexican kitchen serving the Valley since 1968, started by Manuel and Carolina Valenzuela; known for huge fresh flour tortillas (sobaqueras) and machaca burritos. Five locations.

7623.note: Steakhouse and saloon that opened in 1947 on the site of the Phoenix Stockyards, the feedlot cattle baron Edward A. Tovrea established in 1919; restored in 2004.

8195.note: Valley Mexican chain dating to 1946. Founder Woody Johnson said he invented the chimichanga in 1946 at Woody's El Nido, the restaurant that became Macayo's (a claim; El Charro Café in Tucson makes a competing one). This entry is the Ahwatukee (Phoenix) location.
8195.fn: Brand dates to 1946; the original Central Avenue building is gone.

9085.note: Old Town Scottsdale Indigenous gastropub, reported as Native-owned at its 2024 opening (KJZZ); founder Heather Tracy, chef Darryl Montana (Tohono O'odham, per Phoenix magazine).

9240.note: Old Town Scottsdale restaurant serving since 1947.
9240.fn: Serving since 1947; the source doesn't say it has always been at this address.

9684.note: Taco shop from the family behind Super Burrito and Los Gallos; quesabirria tacos and burros.
